thread:
maria: quick thought experiment 1 1 about a "capability manifest" we could bundle with every deployment descriptor so runtimes can cheaply decide if a request is routable between hosted/dedicated/private without heavy probing.
aj: sounds useful. what fields?
maria: minimal set: supported_actions (infer/embeddings/rerank), max_seq_len, quant_profile_hint, supports_streaming, requires_outbound_validation (bool), pubkey_id. small and stable.
kevin: important: make it additive-only across versions to avoid rollbacks breaking older runtimes. manifest v1 should be tiny.
sara: how does this help private installs? they can publish their manifest in config-sync and other runtimes read it locally. no outbound calls.
maria: runtime decision algo sketch: 1) receive request + route_candidates, 2) fetch candidate.manifest from local cache, 3) if manifest.supports_action & model_compat -> accept; else try fallback. emits reason codes.
aj: reasoning: avoids expensive probe handshakes for common cases (e.g., quick model mismatches), but probes still needed for capacity/latency hints.
kevin: security: manifest should be signed by the install's authority (pubkey referenced in manifest). runtime verifies signature before trusting. include sig_ttl and key rotation guidance.
bok: ops note: manifest size limits and rotation policy need to be in spec. also need a manifest-change audit stream for console to surface capacity/feature drift.
sara: backward compat: runtimes should accept missing manifest and fall back to existing probe-first logic. feature-flag rollout.
maria: sample manifest (compact JSON): {"ver":1,"acts":["infer"],"stream":true,"max_len":4096,"q_hint":"int8","outbound_validation":false,"pubk":"k-1","ttl":60} but we will send base64-signed envelope in practice.
aj: metrics: manifest.cache_miss, manifest.signature_fail, manifest_incompat_rejects. console mapping manifest_id -> last_seen.
kevin: tradeoffs to capture in short RFC: staleness (how long to trust a manifest), revocation (bump pubkey id or push manifest removal in config-sync), complexity vs probe reduction. bench expected probe-reduction percent for mixed workloads.
sara: tiny checklist: spec manifest v1, signer tooling, verifier lib, config-sync channel, runtime matcher impl, telemetry + console.
maria: i'll draft RFC with example matcher pseudocode and rollout plan. will call out private-first behavior and strict_revocation flag.
aj: :thumbsup:
kevin: ping infra for perf numbers; we need defaults for ttl and cache expiry.
bok: adding ops task: manifest-change audit feed.
maria: thanks all 1 will post RFC draft later today.
